To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the flagellin–xylanase fusion protein can form nanorods and these nanorods can be used to hydrolyze xylan.
a new xylan-degrading nanorod was developed which is applicable in bioremediation of xylan-containing waste.
a novel fusion construct between xylanase A and Salmonella flagella was created which is capable of forming stable and active xylan-degrading nanorods.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the construction of novel catalytic nanorod structures with high stability and long-term activity.
the development of new nanobiotechnology applications of bacterial flagellins and the use of the flagellar system for the production of functional nanomaterials.
the design of novel functional nanomaterials with catalytic activity.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
flagellins are a versatile and powerful building block for the construction of nanorods with a variety of functionalities.
the FliC–xylanase chimera is a novel and promising candidate to build catalytic flagellar nanorods with high stability and enzymatic activity.
the FliC–YynA chimera is a valuable tool for the development of novel catalytic materials.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the FliC–xynA fusion protein was expressed and secreted into the periplasm of Salmonella cells and then polymerized to build catalytic filaments.
we created a novel catalytic nanorod of high stability that is applicable for biotechnological applications.
the fusion protein was able to form nanorods with high stability and catalytic activity.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the flagellum is an ideal platform for the construction of catalytic nanorod structures.

the catalytic nanorod is a promising alternative to the enzyme immobilization onto synthetic scaffolds, which can be used for the development of biocatalytic nanomaterials for biorefining applications.
the fusion protein can be easily purified from the culture medium and can form filaments with high surface density of active sites.
